77063.subject:
Harness vs Loop vs Graph engineering; Your Transformation Has Too
 Many KPIs!
77063.body:
AI Frontier

Автор: Steve Nouri


Автор: Steve Nouri

    
    
    Прочитайте цю статтю на LinkedIn, щоб приєднатися до обговорення
Прочитати на LinkedIn
https://www.linkedin.com/comm/pulse/harness-vs-loop-graph-engineering-your-transformation-steve-nouri-aaqnc?lipi=urn%3Ali%3Apage%3Aemail_email_series_follow_newsletter_02%3BEVNEdeYERUehIJxrs9YSfA%3D%3D&midToken=AQFTjFOONAfT2w&midSig=2LMHKOPMB1dso1&trk=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_&trkEmail=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_-null-fz96fz~mshhbna0~7m-null-null&eid=fz96fz-mshhbna0-7m
  
AI Agents Need More Than a Good Model Most teams still talk about AI agents as though they are a single technology. But once an agent starts accessing files, calling APIs, writing code, interacting with customers or operating inside business systems, the model is only one component. You are no longer simply prompting an LLM. You are designing a system. Three engineering layers are commonly mixed together: Harness engineering Loop engineering Graph engineering They all improve agent reliability, but they solve different problems. A useful way to remember the difference is: Environment → Feedback → Flow The harness creates the operating environment. The loop determines how work is checked and improved. The graph controls what is allowed to happen next. 1. Harness Engineering: Can the Agent Operate? A harness is everything surrounding the model that allows it to perform useful work. This can include: Tools and APIs Memory and session state File and code workspaces Permissions Model selection Timeouts and budgets Approval gates Logs and traces Two teams can use the same model and get completely different results. One team gives the model clean tools, structured context, durable state and observable execution. The other gives it a large prompt, unreliable tools and excessive permissions. The model is the same. The working conditions are not. Diagnose a harness problem when: The agent cannot access the right tool It forgets progress between sessions It has too much permission Its actions cannot be audited It cannot recover after interruption A good harness is not the one with the most tools. It is the one with the fewest tools required to complete the task safely and consistently. 2. Loop Engineering: Can the Agent Improve Its Work? A loop defines what happens after the model produces an answer or performs an action. A useful loop needs: A specific goal Current state Allowed actions Evidence of success Actionable feedback A stop condition The most important rule is: Do not loop on confidence. Loop on evidence. “The agent believes the task is complete” is not evidence. Better completion conditions include: Tests pass The output matches a schema Citations resolve A policy check succeeds A reviewer approves Required data fields are complete Prompting improves one response. Loop engineering improves the process that produces the response. Exampl
